contention: sustained 18-42 headless_shell / loadavg 15-28 for the entire dispatch — never dropped below 8. Static/data work done first per rule 21; live verification taken in short single-browser windows (boot-check, stl-probe are module-level and browser-light; two stl-live.mjs attempts, first killed by a 240s timeout under load, second completed clean).

Verified the W1-04-r2 finding still held at e97347f, then wired it, and found a second half of the same defect nobody had named: indoor L was skyAmbient(env), so a windowless cellar read L=0.75 at noon and 0.09 at 03:00, flat across the whole floor, in all 115 interiors.

what_landed.what: StealthCrime.syncInteriorLights(sim) mirrors sim.settlements.interior(sim.env.interior).lights into the LightField. That is the SAME record render/interior.js is handed as `rec` and draws rec.lights from — one list, read twice, no copy to drift. The renderer's dedupe (round each axis to a decimetre) is reproduced verbatim so a shared hearth declared by three property zones is one source, not three. Sources are tagged world:true and rebuilt only on a cell change, so a snuffed lamp stays snuffed while you are in the room with it.
what_landed.measured: archon-apothecary: 0 world sources outside -> 8 inside (10 declared, 8 distinct, 7 snuffable). Census over 30 lamplit interiors: mean 6.97 sources/room, mean L spread 0.724, 0/30 rooms flat. Every interior in every previous build had spread exactly 0.

what_landed.what: p.zone is null in all 115 interiors (nothing in the running world sets it) and system.js line 183 therefore gave every interior skyAmbient(env). Guarded on _interiorLit, which is true only when the cell switch actually FOUND the interior record, so an arena or a hand-built W1-07 cell gets exactly the sky it got before.
what_landed.measured: the same point in the room now reads 1.0000 at noon and 1.0000 at 03:00 (a lamp does not care what time it is); before, the whole room read 0.7500 and 0.0900.

what_landed.what: game/data/stealth/detection.json interior_lamps. authored_intensity_to_L_scale 9.3275 and reach_m {flame 9, hearth 18} are both derived from RI-STL01 §3's OWN table (its two torchlit-interior rows and the fact that its last interior row stops at 9 m), NOT from the renderer's x9/x22 and 11/22 m. The 'flame' of those rows is read as the room's HEARTH rather than a wall sconce, which is why the mean is divided by the authored hearth weight 0.9.
what_landed.declared_divergence: render/interior.js caps ILLUMINATING lamps at LIT_CAP=5 and builds the rest as unlit fittings; the sim lights every deduped lamp. That cap is a rendering budget, not a world fact, so it is not copied — recorded in the data file as known_divergence_from_the_renderer. A room with >5 deduped lamps is simulated slightly brighter than it is drawn. Closing it needs the cap in shared data and render/interior.js is W1-04's.

what_landed.what: StealthCrime.asleepInWorld(sim,npc): a person at `home` between 23:00 and 06:00. The world's 1,700-odd authored schedule rows take eight `activity` values and NONE of them is sleep, so nothing in the build could tell a resident in bed from a resident in the doorway and a 03:00 burglary was watched by every resident of the house with a full cone and a clear cast. Derived from the schedule the world already publishes; a sleeper still decays suspicion so somebody who goes to bed having seen something settles rather than freezing at ALARM. spawnCivilian({asleep:true}) lets a scenario state the case, and civTraceBlock reports which.

findings_for_the_critic: THE CONCURRENCY LOSS, and it is the most important line here. Mid-run, THREE of my engine.js edits (spawnProp's property_instance, _furnishInterior's pointer, and takeProp's whole theft routing plus _propertyHas) were SILENTLY REMOVED from the working tree by a neighbour's write — grep found zero occurrences of code that had passed boot-check twenty minutes earlier, in a region another agent (readables/interiors) is mid-edit in. Caught only because the live probe threw `E._propertyHas is not a function`. Re-applied and re-verified. A critic should re-grep game/src/engine.js for `_propertyHas` and `property_instance` before trusting any theft-chain number in this file; if they are gone again, the fix was lost, not wrong.

THE FENCE'S SETTLEMENT REFUSAL IS DEAD FOR NPC-OWNED GOODS. Engine.fenceQuote() passes `world = { npcById: () => null }`, so theft.js::willBuy cannot resolve the owner of `npc:archon-priest-4` to a settlement or a faction and its same_settlement / same_faction / friend_of_the_owner refusals can never fire for anything owned by a PERSON — which is every one of the 1,878 property objects and all 72 new rows. Measured: fence.archon.salvage (owner's own settlement) quoted the stolen item at 25 g exactly as three out-of-town fences did, and identically to a clean-item control. The r2 verdict scored 'ownership enforcement 8' and 'fencing 8' partly on those refusal lines; they are authored, they are in crime-audit FNC-4, and they are unreachable in play. THIS IS THE GAP I WOULD NAME IF I WERE THE CRITIC.

THE INTERIORS ARE OVER-LAMPED. Census: 23 of 30 lamplit rooms have NO floor at all below L 0.10, and the mean dark share is 0.3%. The spread is real (0.724) so the model discriminates, but 'find a dark corner' is not a strategy indoors — 'snuff a lamp' is (7 of 8 in the test room are snuffable, and snuffing one took V from 1.30 to 0.60). Lamp count and placement are W1-04's generator's, not this piece's, and I deliberately did NOT tune the light model until the shipped rooms looked right — that would be fitting the instrument to the fixture.

TRESPASS ZONES ARE STILL NEVER ENTERED. p.zone is null in every one of the 115 interiors because nothing in the running world ever sets it; trespassCheck() is a harness verb taking a zone id. So zone context multipliers, zone baselines and the whole shop_closed/dwelling trespass ladder (which W1-15-r3's earlier pass fixed for 66/66 zones) still have no world-side producer. I did not fix this: deriving p.zone from the player's position inside an interior's property zone bounds is the obvious next change and it belongs with whoever owns the zone->interior mapping.

GUARDS ARE ALWAYS FULL WITNESSES (guards_always_full_witnesses: true, guard_V_min 0.05), so the guard I placed 20 m outside the room to receive the report also became a witness on every arm — witnesses 2, routes [shout, guard_witness]. That is the shipped rule working, but it means 'a witness ran and told a guard' and 'a guard saw it himself' are hard to separate in an artifact.

The round-2 verdict's biggest_gap (GAP-W1-crime-enforcement-is-a-free-win: guard_legion cannot attack and its parley surrendered for free) is STILL only half closed — the predecessor raised gold_price 0 -> 300 and left the AI and the disposition floor. I did not touch it either, for the same reason: it is combat/enemy.js and combat/parley.js, both owned elsewhere and both under concurrent edit.
